rationale: This is an incremental respecification of the archived "Equity-Funded Overhead Burden" whose second term is now dominated by −oancf/at, collapsing the signal toward the already-tested "equity issuance by cash-poor firms" channel (cf. Cash-Strained Equity Recycling) rather than isolating an overhead funding gap.

Adding xint — typically an order of magnitude smaller than dlc — to the archived "Maturity Funding Gap" numerator is a cosmetic perturbation that will produce a signal nearly collinear with the original rather than a distinct economic test.

The construction is internally consistent (high repurchase intensity times cash-backed earnings loads positive) and the sign-reversal test against the accrual-financing result is economically motivated, though it partly rides the well-documented accruals anomaly conditioned on payout and overlaps in spirit with the archived Cash-Matched Buyback.

Substituting an operating-cash-flow trend for the gross-margin trend is a defensible, diagnosis-driven fix that ties the conditioner directly to dividend funding capacity, but it remains a single-variable swap on an archived signal rather than a new mechanism.

Recasting the R&D interaction from funding source to per-share commercialization outcome is a genuinely different mechanism, the nonnegative rank times signed growth preserves the intended direction, and the main caveat is instability of GROWTH on a per-share ratio for small-csho or low-margin firms.

(oancf − Δlt)/at is essentially the sum of two long-established anomalies — cash-flow-to-assets profitability and the balance-sheet/financing (liability growth) effect — so it is a linear rediscovery rather than a cross-theme interaction.
